title: AI-assisted code review checklist
summary: Use this checklist to evaluate AI-assisted code changes before approving or merging them. It keeps the review tied to requirements, observable evidence, security concerns, and documented decisions.
prerequisites: The proposed code change and its stated purpose
The relevant requirements and repository review rules
Access to the checks normally used for the affected code

sections.title: Review checklist
paragraphs: How should a practitioner review an AI-assisted code change? Use the following intermediate-level checklist and approve the change only when each applicable check has evidence or a documented resolution.

Check 1: Confirm the intended behavior, affected components, and acceptance conditions before examining implementation details. If the purpose or scope is unclear, pause the review and ask the change owner to supply or clarify them.

Check 2: Compare every changed area with the stated requirements, including error paths, boundary conditions, and interactions with unchanged code. If the change is too large to trace reliably, request that it be divided into smaller reviewable units or arrange an additional focused review.

Check 3: Treat AI-generated explanations and review suggestions as unverified until they agree with the code and observable evidence. If a claim cannot be confirmed, exclude it from the approval basis and ask for reproducible evidence or direct human analysis.

Check 4: Run the applicable automated and manual checks for the affected behavior, then inspect the results rather than relying on a success summary. If a required check cannot run, record the reason and obtain equivalent evidence or keep the review unresolved.

Check 5: Examine input handling, permissions, sensitive data exposure, failure behavior, and changed dependencies where they apply. If the reviewer cannot determine the security impact, escalate the affected area to a person qualified to assess it before approval.

Check 6: Record each material finding with its location, evidence, requested action, and disposition. If a finding lacks enough detail for another person to reproduce it, add the missing context before assigning or closing it.

Check 7: Make the final decision from the reviewed change and collected evidence, not from the AI system's confidence or wording. If required evidence is absent or a material finding remains unresolved, do not approve the change; return it for correction or explicitly escalate the decision.

sections.title: Source correction
paragraphs: The cited source changed during this update. The previous citation pointed to content/resources/coding-agents/ai-assisted-code-review-checklist.json, the same unregistered local resource being reviewed, and it had never been verified. It was replaced with the official secure software development framework publication from the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

This correction affects the source attribution and verification record. The replacement source supports reviewing human-readable code for vulnerabilities and compliance with security requirements. The checklist procedure remains provider-neutral and does not depend on a named tool, version, or configuration.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the stated purpose and scope, the reviewed change, results from applicable checks, records of material findings, resolutions or escalation notes, and the final review decision.

Verify completion by confirming that every applicable checklist item points to observable evidence and that every non-applicable item has a reason. Confirm that another reviewer can reproduce the decision from the record. If evidence is missing, contradictory, or not reproducible, reopen the relevant check and obtain the missing evidence before approval.
